title: Polity Complete 4: Local Government, Tribal Areas, Bodies & Elections

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:
1. It inserted Part IX containing Articles 243 to 243O.
2. It added the Eleventh Schedule containing 18 functional items for Panchayats.
3. It came into force on 24 April 1993.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Part IX (Arts 243 to 243O) was inserted and the Act took effect on 24 April 1993. The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects; 18 is the number in the Twelfth Schedule for Municipalities.
questions.h: 73rd = 29 (Eleventh), 74th = 18 (Twelfth): reverse order of the Amendment numbers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Municipalities under Part IXA:
1. A Nagar Panchayat is constituted for a transitional area.
2. A Municipal Council is constituted for a larger urban area.
3. Wards Committees are to be constituted in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more.
4. The Metropolitan Planning Committee is provided for in Article 243ZD.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 243Q: Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area, Municipal Council for a smaller urban area and Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area; Art 243S requires Wards Committees at 3 lakh population. Art 243ZD is the District Planning Committee; the Metropolitan Planning Committee is Art 243ZE.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about reservation in Panchayats under Article 243D:
1. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population in the Panchayat area.
2. Not less than one-third of the total seats are reserved for women, including women belonging to SC and ST.
3. Reservation of seats for Other Backward Classes is mandatory under the Article.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 243D(1) and (2) give proportional SC/ST seats and one-third women seats (including within SC/ST). Reservation for backward classes is left to the State Legislature, so it is not mandatory.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of committees and their recommendations on Panchayati Raj:
1. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee: Three-tier structure of Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad
2. Ashok Mehta Committee: Two-tier structure of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat
3. G.V.K. Rao Committee: Block as the basic unit of planning and development
4. L.M. Singhvi Committee: Constitutional recognition of Panchayati Raj institutions
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985) made the district the basic unit of planning, calling for a post of District Development Commissioner. The other three pairs are correct, and Singhvi's 1986 push led towards the 73rd Amendment.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Part IX of the Constitution on Panchayats extends automatically to the Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas.
Statement-II: Article 243M(4) allows Parliament to extend Part IX to Scheduled Areas by law, with exceptions and modifications.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Art 243M(4) excludes Scheduled and tribal areas from Part IX unless Parliament extends it by law, so Statement-I is incorrect. Parliament did extend it with modifications through PESA 1996, so Statement-II is correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following urban local bodies is NOT constituted under Part IXA of the Constitution?
questions.e: Art 243Q recognises Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation. A Cantonment Board is created by the Cantonments Act 2006 and is administered by the Ministry of Defence.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA:
1. It superintends elections to Panchayats only, while municipal elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India.
2. The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.
3. The State Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds applicable to a Judge of a High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 243K(2) and 243K(1): the Governor appoints the Commissioner, who is removable only like a High Court Judge. The same State Election Commission handles both Panchayat (243K) and Municipal (243ZA) elections.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Gram Sabha is a body of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the area of a Panchayat.
2. The powers and functions of the Gram Sabha are those that the State Legislature provides by law.
3. Panchayats at the intermediate level need not be constituted in a State with a population not exceeding 40 lakh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Arts 243(b) and 243A define the Gram Sabha and leave its powers to the State Legislature. The intermediate tier may be skipped only where the population does not exceed 20 lakh, not 40 lakh (Art 243B(2)).

questions.q: According to Article 243ZD, what proportion of the members of the District Planning Committee is to be elected by the elected members of the district-level Panchayat and the Municipalities in the district from amongst themselves?
questions.e: Four-fifths of the members are elected in proportion to the rural and urban population of the district. The Committee then consolidates the plans of Panchayats and Municipalities into a draft development plan for the district.

questions.q: The first Panchayati Raj institution in independent India was inaugurated on 2 October 1959 in which one of the following places?
questions.e: Prime Minister Nehru inaugurated it at Nagaur, Rajasthan, putting the Balwant Rai Mehta three-tier scheme into practice. Rajasthan was the first State, followed soon after by Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about State Finance Commissions for Panchayats:
1. The President constitutes the Finance Commission to review the financial position of Panchayats.
2. The Union Finance Commission is to recommend measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State based on the State Finance Commission's recommendations.
3. The recommendations of the State Finance Commission are binding on the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Art 243I makes the Governor, not the President, constitute the Commission every fifth year, and Art 280(3)(bb) links the Union Commission to it. Its recommendations are advisory; the Governor lays an action-taken report before the Legislature.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tribes Advisory Council under the Fifth Schedule:
1. It is established in each State having Scheduled Areas.
2. It consists of not more than twenty members, of whom, as nearly as may be, three-fourths are representatives of Scheduled Tribes in the State Legislative Assembly.
3. The Governor declares areas as Scheduled Areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Para 4 of the Fifth Schedule provides the Council with up to 20 members, with three-fourths from the ST members of the Assembly. Para 6 gives the power to declare Scheduled Areas to the President, not the Governor.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q: Under the general scheme of the Sixth Schedule, an Autonomous District Council consists of
o: not more than 30 members, of whom not more than four are nominated by the Governor and the rest elected on adult suffrage
not more than 40 members, of whom six are nominated by the President
30 members, all elected on adult suffrage with no nominated members
not more than 30 members, all nominated by the Governor from tribal leaders
questions.e: Para 2 provides an elected body with a small nominated element. Councils are elected for five years, and their powers are administrative, judicial and legislative on listed subjects.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT an Autonomous District Council under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution?
o: Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council, Leh
questions.e: The Sixth Schedule covers Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, with 10 councils in all (Chakma is in Mizoram). The Leh council was set up by a separate law and is not under the Sixth Schedule.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996:
1. It followed the recommendations of the Bhuria Committee.
2. It enables the Gram Sabha to safeguard the traditions and customs of the people and their cultural identity.
3. It applies to the Sixth Schedule areas of the north-east.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PESA flowed from the 1995 Bhuria Committee and strengthens the Gram Sabha. It covers the Fifth Schedule areas of ten States, not the Sixth Schedule areas, which have their own councils.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Governor can direct that an Act of Parliament or of the State Legislature shall not apply to a Scheduled Area or shall apply with modifications.
Statement-II: The Governor may make regulations for peace and good government of a Scheduled Area, including on transfer of land by Scheduled Tribe members, subject to the President's assent.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are Para 5 powers: para 5(1) is the power to direct non-application of laws, and 5(2) and 5(3) deal with regulations needing the President's assent. They are two separate powers, so the second does not explain the first.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following was constituted as an 'autonomous State within the State of Assam' before becoming a full State in 1972?
questions.e: Art 244A, inserted by the 22nd Amendment 1969, allowed an autonomous State within Assam, and Meghalaya was formed as one in 1970. It became a full State in January 1972.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Article 244(1): Administration of Scheduled Areas in States other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
2. Article 275(1): Grants-in-aid to States for tribal welfare and Scheduled Area administration
3. Article 339(1): Commission on administration of Scheduled Areas, appointed at the end of ten years from the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at any time
4. Article 342: List of Scheduled Tribes of a State specified by the Governor
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Art 342 empowers the President, after consulting the Governor for a State, to specify the Scheduled Tribes, and only Parliament can alter the list. The other three pairs are correct.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q: In Orissa Mining Corporation v. Ministry of Environment and Forests (2013), concerning the Niyamgiri hills, the Supreme Court directed that
o: the mining project could proceed on State Government approval alone
the Forest Advisory Committee would take the final decision on tribal rights
Gram Sabhas should decide whether the project affected the religious and cultural rights of the Dongria Kondh community under the Forest Rights Act
the National Green Tribunal should hold public hearings in each village
questions.e: The Court gave the Gram Sabhas the decisive role under the Forest Rights Act, 2006. This is a landmark in recognising community rights over forests in tribal areas.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sixth Schedule:
1. The Governor may appoint a commission to examine and report on the administration of autonomous districts.
2. Laws made by a District Council require the President's assent.
3. District Councils can make laws on marriage and divorce and social customs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Para 14 gives the commission power to the Governor, and Para 3 lets Councils legislate on social customs, marriage and divorce. Their laws take effect on the Governor's assent, not the President's.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q: The 94th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2006 relates to
o: a Minister in charge of tribal welfare in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, exempting Bihar
reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in private educational institutions
the creation of a National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
inclusion of Bodo in the Eighth Schedule
questions.e: It amended the proviso to Art 164(1) to cover Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand (along with Madhya Pradesh and Odisha) and removed Bihar. Private institutions were the 93rd, the NCST the 89th and Bodo the 92nd.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Scheduled and Tribal Areas chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of Article and State is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Art 371J, inserted by the 98th Amendment 2012, gives special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region of Karnataka. Maharashtra and Gujarat are covered by Art 371(2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies under Article 334 has been extended to 2030.
2. Nomination of the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies under Articles 331 and 333 has ended.
3. Article 334 also governs reservation of seats for Other Backward Classes in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST seat reservation by ten years from January 2020 and ended Anglo-Indian nomination. Art 334 contains no OBC seat reservation in legislatures.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Parliament inserted Article 16(4A) to permit reservation in promotions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Statement-II: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), the Supreme Court held that reservation under Article 16(4) cannot be extended to promotions.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 77th Amendment 1995 inserted Art 16(4A) to undo the effect of the Indra Sawhney bar on promotion quotas. The verdict is thus the cause of the amendment.
questions.h: Court says no (1992), Parliament says yes (1995).

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct regarding the reservation for Economically Weaker Sections introduced by the 103rd Amendment?
o: It is available to economically weak Scheduled Castes in addition to their existing quota
It inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) into the Constitution
It was struck down by the Supreme Court in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India
It raised the overall cap on reservations to 60 per cent in the Constitution
questions.e: The Amendment inserted Arts 15(6) and 16(6) for classes not covered by the existing reservations, so SC, ST and OBC are excluded. The Supreme Court upheld it in Janhit Abhiyan (2022), and the 50 per cent ceiling was never in the constitutional text.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Eighth Schedule:
1. Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment Act, 1967.
2. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment Act, 1992.
3. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment Act, 2003.
4. The name 'Odia' was substituted for 'Oriya' by the 96th Amendment Act, 2011.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct, and together they explain how the Schedule grew from 14 languages to the present 22. Remember the sequence of additions: Sindhi, then three in 1992, then four in 2003.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of Article and subject is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 346: Official language for communication between one State and another
Article 347: Special provision relating to language spoken by a section of the population of a State
Article 349: Language to be used in the proceedings of Parliament
Article 351: Directive for the development of the Hindi language
questions.e: Article 349 lays down a special procedure for enacting laws relating to language, needing the President's previous sanction. The language of Parliamentary proceedings is dealt with in Article 120.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets lists the languages that were accorded classical language status by the Union Cabinet in October 2024?
o: Marathi, Konkani, Assamese, Bengali and Maithili
Pali, Prakrit, Sindhi, Bengali and Marathi
Bengali, Assamese, Bodo, Pali and Marathi
Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali
questions.e: Five languages were added in October 2024, taking the total classical languages to eleven. The earlier six were Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Odia.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:
1. Article 324 provides that the number of Election Commissioners, if any, shall be fixed by the President from time to time.
2. The Constitution fixes the number of Election Commissioners at two.
3. The Chief Election Commissioner holds office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier, under the 2023 Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 324(2) leaves the size of the Commission to the President, which is why the Commission has moved between one and three members. The Constitution does not fix two Commissioners.

questions.q: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, the selection committee for recommending appointments to the President comprises
o: the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India
the Prime Minister, the Home Minister and the Chief Justice of India
the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
the Vice-President, the Speaker and the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
questions.e: The Supreme Court, in Anoop Baranwal (March 2023), set up an interim committee with the Chief Justice of India until Parliament legislated. The 2023 Act then replaced the Chief Justice with a Union Cabinet Minister.
questions.h: Baranwal bench had the CJI; the Act swapped him for a Cabinet Minister.

questions.q:
Statement-I: A sitting Member of Parliament or State Legislature who is convicted and sentenced to imprisonment of two years or more is disqualified from the date of conviction.
Statement-II: In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which had allowed sitting legislators to continue for three months after conviction pending appeal.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Section 8(3) disqualifies on conviction with a sentence of two years or more. Earlier, Section 8(4) shielded sitting members, and its removal in 2013 is what makes the disqualification immediate.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 329:
1. It bars the courts from questioning the validity of a law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats.
2. It provides that an election to Parliament or a State Legislature can be questioned only by an election petition.
3. Once the election process has begun, courts can freely intervene by writ petition on any irregularity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 329(a) and (b) bar court interference in delimitation laws and give election petitions as the exclusive remedy. In N.P. Ponnuswami (1952), the Supreme Court held that the process should not be disrupted midway.

questions.q: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 relates to
o: reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha
freezing delimitation of constituencies until after the 2026 Census
reducing the voting age from 21 years to 18 years
questions.e: It amended Article 326, widening the electorate with younger voters from 1989. The freezing of delimitation was done by the 84th Amendment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about delimitation:
1. The Delimitation Commission is appointed by the Election Commission of India.
2. The 84th Amendment froze the total number of Lok Sabha and Assembly seats until the first Census taken after 2026.
3. Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be questioned before any court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Delimitation Commission is appointed by the Central Government under the Delimitation Act, not by the Election Commission. Its orders have the force of law and, in line with Article 329(a), are immune from judicial challenge.

questions.q:
Statement-I: A civil servant may be dismissed without an inquiry where he has been convicted on a criminal charge.
Statement-II: Article 311(2) exempts conviction on a criminal charge, impracticability of holding an inquiry, and security of the State from the requirement of an inquiry.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The safeguard of a reasonable opportunity to be heard in Article 311(2) has these three exceptions. Conviction is one of them, so no separate inquiry is needed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about All-India Services:
1. Creation of a new All-India Service requires a resolution of the Lok Sabha supported by two-thirds of members present and voting.
2. The Indian Forest Service was created in 1966 under Article 312.
3. The services known as IAS and IPS at the commencement of the Constitution are deemed to be services created by Parliament under Article 312.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 312 the resolution must come from the Rajya Sabha, as it represents the States, not from the Lok Sabha. Article 312(2) deems IAS and IPS to be Parliament-created, and the Forest Service was added in 1966.

questions.q:
Statement-I: After the L. Chandra Kumar judgment, Administrative Tribunals under Article 323A are free from the High Courts' writ jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227.
Statement-II: In L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court held that judicial review is part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Court held that excluding the High Courts' jurisdiction was invalid, so tribunal decisions are subject to High Court scrutiny. Statement-I is therefore wrong, while the basic-structure reasoning in Statement-II is right.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 323A empowers State Legislatures to establish administrative tribunals for public service matters.
2. Article 323B empowers Parliament and State Legislatures to establish tribunals for matters such as taxation, industrial disputes and land reforms.
3. Articles 323A and 323B were inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 323A allows only Parliament to create administrative tribunals for public service matters. Both Articles came from the 42nd Amendment, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the National Green Tribunal?
o: Its Principal Bench sits at Pune
It is not bound by the procedure of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and is guided by principles of natural justice
It can hear any dispute involving the environment arising under any law
Appeals against its orders lie to the High Court
questions.e: The 2010 Act frees it from the CPC and the Evidence Act, with natural justice as the guide. It hears matters under seven listed environmental laws, its Principal Bench is at Delhi, and appeals go to the Supreme Court.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission:
1. It is a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
2. The Chairperson can be a person who has been the Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court.
3. The Chairperson and members can be removed by the President on the grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
4. Its recommendations are binding on the Government.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2019 amendment widened the Chairperson's eligibility to any former Judge of the Supreme Court. The Commission's recommendations are advisory, so Statement 4 is wrong.

questions.q: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Prime Minister is
o: entirely outside the jurisdiction of the Lokpal
within the jurisdiction of the Lokpal in all matters without exception
within the jurisdiction of the Lokpal, except for allegations relating to international relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space
within the jurisdiction of the Lokpal only after he has left office
questions.e: The Act includes the Prime Minister but excludes these sensitive subjects. An inquiry against a serving Prime Minister needs the approval of at least two-thirds of the Lokpal bench and is held in camera.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission:
1. It was given statutory status in 2003 by an Act of Parliament.
2. It is a constitutional body under Article 324A.
3. It exercises superintendence over the CBI in respect of investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Commission began in 1964 on the Santhanam Committee's advice and became statutory in 2003. There is no Article 324A in the Constitution.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Zonal Councils:
1. They are constitutional bodies.
2. The Union Home Minister is the common Chairman of all the Zonal Councils.
3. The north-eastern States are part of a Zonal Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The five Zonal Councils are statutory bodies created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, not constitutional ones. The north-eastern States come under the separate North Eastern Council set up by the 1971 Act.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union Public Service Commission:
1. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President.
2. The Constitution specifies the number of its members.
3. A member of the UPSC is eligible for appointment as Chairman of the UPSC or of a State Public Service Commission.
4. The Chairman of the UPSC is eligible for further employment under the Government of India after retirement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 316 gives appointment to the President, while Article 316 and the 1969 order of the President fix numbers, not the Constitution. The Chairman is barred from further Government employment, while a member may be made Chairman of the UPSC or a SPSC.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
o: He is appointed by the President
He audits the accounts of the Union and the States
His salary and service conditions can be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment
He can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds applicable to a Judge of the Supreme Court
questions.e: Article 148(3) protects the CAG's salary and conditions, which cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment. This and the Supreme Court judge-like removal secure his independence.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
1. It is a constitutional body that replaced the Planning Commission.
2. Its Governing Council includes the Chief Ministers of all States.
3. The Vice-Chairperson holds the rank of a Cabinet Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NITI Aayog was set up by a Union Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015, so it is neither constitutional nor statutory. Its Governing Council has the Chief Ministers of all States and the Vice-Chairperson has Cabinet rank.

questions.q:
Arrange the following bodies in the chronological order of their establishment:
1. Planning Commission
2. First Finance Commission
3. NITI Aayog
4. Central Vigilance Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Planning Commission was set up in 1950 and the first Finance Commission followed in 1951. The CVC came in 1964 and NITI Aayog in 2015.

questions.q: Article 371J of the Constitution provides special provisions for
questions.e: Inserted by the 98th Amendment 2012, it provides a regional development board and reservation in education and jobs for the region. The Vidarbha and Marathwada boards are under Article 371(2).

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the President to appoint a Commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes?
questions.e: Article 340 is the source of both the Kalelkar and Mandal Commissions. Article 341 deals with the list of Scheduled Castes.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The 105th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2021 restored the power of States and Union Territories to prepare their own list of socially and educationally backward classes.
Statement-II: In the Maratha reservation case (Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil, 2021), the Supreme Court held that after the 102nd Amendment only the President and Parliament could identify such classes.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 102nd Amendment inserted Article 342A and the 2021 judgment read it as taking away the States' power. The 105th Amendment was passed to undo that outcome.
